context: A teacher walks a student through a famous court case for an essay
purpose: Teach: 検察/最高裁/警察官/制裁/疑惑/不当/警戒/衝突

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 今日はレポートの題材になっている裁判について一緒に整理しましょうか。
lines.en: Today let's organize the trial you're using as your report topic.
lines.style: Calm composed teacher voice, gentle guiding tone, measured pace, warm encouraging delivery

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、最初に検察がどんな証拠を出したのかが、よく分からなくて。
lines.en: Yes, I don't really understand what evidence the prosecution presented first.
lines.style: Earnest university student, slightly hesitant, thinking out loud, polite respectful tone

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 当時、被告には汚職疑惑があって、現役の警察官まで巻き込まれた大きな事件だったの。
lines.en: At the time the defendant faced corruption allegations, even involving an active police officer in a huge case.
lines.style: Explanatory teacher mode, slower clearer enunciation, slightly serious historical recounting

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: なるほど。それで世間の警戒も一気に強まったんですね。
lines.en: I see, so public vigilance suddenly heightened because of that.
lines.style: Connecting the dots aloud, curious engaged student, rising comprehension in his voice

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: そう。報道と捜査機関の見解が真っ向から衝突して、世論も二分されたわ。
lines.en: Exactly. The media and investigators' views clashed head-on and public opinion split in two.
lines.style: Thoughtful reflective delivery, slight gravity, illustrating tension with measured emphasis

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 判決そのものは、最終的に最高裁まで行ったって本に書いてありました。
lines.en: The verdict itself eventually went all the way to the Supreme Court, the book said.
lines.style: Citing source confidently, slightly proud he researched it, conversational academic tone

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: そうね。下級審の不当な判断が覆されて、結果的に制裁の内容も大きく変わったの。
lines.en: Right, the lower court's unjust ruling was overturned and the sanctions ultimately changed significantly.
lines.style: Authoritative summary, teacher delivering key insight, deliberate emphasis on turning point

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: じゃあ、その逆転の理由を中心にエッセイを書けば説得力が出そうですね。
lines.en: Then if I center my essay on the reasons for that reversal it should be persuasive.
lines.style: Sudden clarity, motivated student forming a plan, slightly excited and resolved

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: いい着眼点よ。判例の引用も忘れずにね、頑張って。
lines.en: Excellent angle. Don't forget to cite the precedents — good luck.
lines.style: Encouraging closing remark, warm smile audible in voice, supportive mentor energy
